CT-7567, nicknamed Rex, was the gruff, no-nonsense leader of the 501st Legion<ref name="TCWCG">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref> and [[Torrent Company/Legends|Torrent Company]] during the early stages of the Clone Wars.<ref name="TCWn" /> His abilities of leadership and confidence were spotted early by the Kaminoan cloners, and he went through additional rigorous training<ref name="TCWTVG" /> in a variety of tactics and fighting styles<ref name="TCWCG" /> to enhance his abilities,<ref name="TCWTVG" /> emerging to eventually hold the reputation as one of the toughest clones in the galaxy.<ref name="TCWCG" /> Having displayed himself in battle, he wore honorific [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Jaig eyes]] on his helmet with his customized armor.<ref name="TCWTVG" /> Serving directly under [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]],<ref name="db" /> he adopted the Jedi's tendencies for unorthodox combat strategies and tactics.<ref name="TCWCG" /> He led the 501st in many battles, including ones at Christophsis, Teth,<ref name="TCWn" /> Bothawui,<ref name="Wild Space" /> JanFathal,<ref name="No Prisoners" /> Quell,<ref name="Jedi Crash Ep Guide" /> and Kothlis.<ref name="Gambit: Stealth" /> Rex cared greatly for his men, and was always on the look for clones that showed grit under fire for consideration as potential 501st recruits.<ref name="TCWTVG" />

===Coric===
{{Quote|Agent Devis said to come back for you, sir. An officer's missus always outranks him, so she's like a commodore. And she's in my face.|Coric, to Rex|<ref name="No Prisoners" />}}
{{Main|Coric}}
Coric was a clone trooper trained in both combat and the [[Medic/Legends|medical]] field. Serving in the 501st Legion's Torrent Company, he used his talents to treat injured troops during the Battle of Christophsis, manning the Republic's temporary medical station in Crystal City. The sergeant led a squad at the following Battle of Teth, which saw him emerge as one of the few Torrent Company survivors alongside Captain Rex and five other clones.<ref name="TCWn" /> Coric once again served with Rex on JanFathal, flying the shuttle that the Republic task force used to extract Intelligence Agent Hallena Devis from the world and escape to Captain Gilad Pellaeon's ''Leveler''. During the flight back, the sergeant employed his medical skills to help the injured Ince, but the trooper died shortly after returning to ''Leveler''.<ref name="No Prisoners" /> Coric expressed a dry humor, even in the direst situations, much like Rex himself.<ref name="TCWn" />

===CC-1119===
{{Quote|I was rather fond of Commander Appo.|Darth Vader, on Appo's death|<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader" />}}
{{Main|CC-1119/Legends}}
[[File:Appo.jpg|right|thumb|CC-1119|200px]]
CC-1119, or Appo, was in command of the 501st by 19 BBY.<ref name="ROTS" /> He had trained under the [[Alpha-class Advanced Recon Commando|Alpha-class]] [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|Advanced Recon Commando]] [[Alpha (Advanced Recon Commando)|Alpha-17]].<ref name="Databank Alpha">{{DB|organization|clonetroopers|clone troopers}}</ref> Before rising to the rank of Commander of the 501st Legion, Appo served as a [[Clone Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] in the ranks of the 501st during the Republic [[Battle of Umbara/Legends|campaign on]] [[Umbara/Legends|Umbara]].<ref name="The General" /> When [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] was put into effect in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Appo participated with the rest of the 501st in [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|Operation: Knightfall]]—the utter destruction of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] and the massacre of its occupants. During this mission, he led the legion under the command of the newly-anointed [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. While the operation was still being carried out, Appo was injured by the [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Zett Jukassa/Legends|Zett Jukassa]], who attacked a group of clones, including Appo, as they barred [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Prestor Organa]] from entering. However, Jukassa was killed by Fox, and Appo survived to continue leading the 501st under the orders of Vader.<ref name="ROTS" /> Appo and his men later helped Vader defeat several Jedi at the Kessel conclave,<ref name="Purge" /> and would follow Vader to Murkhana. Following a confrontation with several rebellious clones there, Appo and his men accompanied Vader to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] in hopes of arresting Senator [[Fang Zar/Legends|Fang Zar]] for treason. On Alderaan, Vader was able to fatally injure Zar as he tried to flee, and the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] then led his men to Kashyyyk. Appo was killed by Roan Shryne on Kashyyyk, although Vader then finished off the Jedi while the forests of Kashyyyk burned from Imperial bombardment.<ref name="Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader" />

===CT-0000/1010===
{{Quote|Don't worry about him; let him go!|Fox, ordering his men to cease firing at Bail Organa|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
{{Main|CT-0000/1010/Legends}}
[[File:SergeantFox.jpg|thumb|left|150px|CT-0000/1010]]
CT-0000/1010, also known as Fox, was a sergeant by the time of Order 66. Stationed on Coruscant, he helped establish patrols in the Coruscant underworld to locate [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorists]]. Fox also knew of the Mandalorian [[Journeyman Protector/Legends|Journeyman Protectors]] on [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]], and wished to become one at some point. In 19 BBY, Fox was a member of the squad that stormed the Jedi Temple under the command of Lord Vader, and helped guard the the Council Towers' [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] complex. When Senator Organa arrived during this incident, asking to speak to the Jedi Council and demanding to know what had happened, Appo insisted he leave. When the Padawan Zett Jukassa suddenly attacked the clones, Fox shot and killed him. He then ordered his men to let Organa leave unharmed as the senator fled away in his [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]].<ref name="ROTS" /><ref name="GAR" /><ref name="Order 66: Destroy All Jedi" />

===Retired clone trooper===
{{Quote|After the Kamino uprising, the Emperor decided an army of genetically identical clones was too susceptible to corruption. Future clones would be bred from a variety of templates. Though the 501st itself remained pure, gradually, the rest of the Imperial Army became more and more diverse. We never really got used to the new guys.|Entry from the 501st Journal, composed by the retired clone trooper|<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II" />}}
{{Main|Retired clone trooper}}
This veteran trooper composed a [[501st Journal|journal]] of his thoughts during some of the most well-known battles he had fought during his long service in the Clone Army and later the Imperial Military. A clone of Jango Fett, he was a member of the 501st from its formation, and took part in the Clone Wars and the Galactic Civil War. This trooper recorded entries on the battles of Mygeeto, Felucia, Coruscant, Kashyyyk, Utapau, Naboo, Mustafar, Kamino, Polis Massa, the Death Star, Tantive IV, Yavin, and Hoth.<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II" />

===Daine Jir===
[[File:Dainejir.png|thumb|right|160px|Daine Jir]]
{{Quote|Holding her is dangerous. If word of this gets out, it could generate sympathy for the Rebellion in the Senate.|Daine Jir, to Darth Vader, referring to Leia Organa|<ref name="anh" />}}
{{Main|Daine Jir/Legends}}
Daine Jir was a member of the 501st by 0 BBY. Jir was known as a dedicated, competent officer who was unafraid to speak his mind, even to Darth Vader, a man who normally tolerated no dissent among his soldiers. However, it was said that the Dark Lord appreciated Jir's honesty and even respected Jir.<ref name="tef">{{InsiderCite|96|The Empire's Finest: Who's Who in the Imperial Military}}</ref> In 0 BBY, Jir helped lead the attack on the ''Tantive IV'' above Tatooine. There, the 501st was able to capture Leia Organa, and turn her over to Vader for questioning. Jir warned Vader that holding Organa could be dangerous; if the Senate learned that the Empire had taken one of its own into custody, it could create controversy and even support for the Alliance. However, Vader was unconcerned and ordered Jir to destroy the ''Tantive IV'' and then send a distress signal claiming the ship had been hit by [[Meteorite/Legends|meteorites]].<ref name="anh" />

===Su-mil===
{{Main|Su-mil}}
Su-mil was an [[Eickarie]] member of the 501st from [[Kariek]]. Originally a freedom fighter on his planet, he participated in the [[Capture of the Warlord|Battle of Kariek]] in 22 ABY, in an effort to liberate his planet from the control of [[The Warlord]]. Fighting alongside the 501st, the Eickaries were able to defeat the Warlord. Impressed with the efforts of Su-mil, the trooper [[Jorm Whistler Mackenni]] offered him a position in the squad. Su-mil accepted, and took the name Grappler.<ref name="bargain" /> A member of Unit Aurek-Seven following Mackenni's retirement, he participated in the Battle of the Redoubt against the Vagaari.<ref name="Survivor's Quest" />

===Oron Jaeger===
[[File:Oron_Jaeger.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Oron Jaeger]]
{{Quote|General Oron Jaeger, 501st, commander on Bastion.|Oron Jaeger|<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy 3: Broken, Part 3" />}}
{{Main|Oron Jaeger}}
Oron Jaeger was the commander of the 501st in 137 ABY. Jaeger was injured during the [[Battle of Corulag]], and was fitted with [[Borg Construct Aj^6|cybernetic]] implants during his surgery. The implants made him a cyborg and allowed him to perform various complex tasks at once, such as monitoring communications.<ref name="legacy guide">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Jaeger remained loyal to Emperor Roan Fel after he was [[Attack on Emperor Fel|overthrown]] by the One Sith in 130 ABY, although he did not rebel against Darth Krayt's new government, feigning loyalty until Fel arrived on Bastion and succeeded in taking the planet back from Krayt's supporters. When Lieutenant [[Kiefer]]—who was loyal to Krayt—attempted to kill Fel, Jaeger shot and killed him.<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy 3: Broken, Part 3" />

==Behind the scenes==
The name is a reference to the fan organization known as the [[501st Legion (fan organization)|501st Legion charity group]]. Formed by [[Albin Johnson]] and Tom Crews in [[1997]], it was originally composed of members who wore stormtrooper costumes, and has since expanded to include all trooper variations, as well as [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]], bounty hunters, and other villains from the series. It boasts over 20,000 members in over 65 countries. The 501st Legion helps coordinate volunteers at [[Celebration]], the official ''[[Star Wars]]'' convention. The group also has the nickname "Vader's Fist," which was subsequently also made the in-universe designation for the legion. The honorary leader is [[David Prowse]], the actor who physically portrayed Darth Vader in the original trilogy.

The 501st Legion was first [[canon]]ized in [[2004]] by the novel ''[[Survivor's Quest]]'' and e-book ''[[Fool's Bargain]]'', both written by [[Timothy Zahn]] and released simultaneously. In a further tribute to the real-life organization, the legion of blue clone troopers led by Darth Vader into the Jedi Temple in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] was designated the 501st. Although this name was not mentioned in the film itself, much of the support material and merchandising for the film make this reference, including the video game ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', which first gave backstory to the legion.

===Non-canon===
====''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition''====
{{Quote|Sir, a squad of stormtroopers from the 501st Legion have breached the corridor ahead.|Lieutenant Marsen, to Lord Starkiller|<ref name="USE">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition]]''</ref>}}
The video game ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed: Ultimate Sith Edition]]'' features an alternate timeline that follows the non-[[canon]]ical [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] ending of [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed|''The Force Unleashed'']]. The game features a different take on the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], although the 501st Legion is still deployed to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] just as they had been in the canonical version of the battle. After infiltrating [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]], a [[Squad/Legends|squad]] of 501st [[Cold assault stormtrooper|snowtroopers]] are ambushed by [[Rebel trooper/Legends|Rebel troopers]] in one of the corridors near the main hangar.<ref name="USE" />

At the same time, [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Galen Marek|Starkiller]]—[[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] and successor of the [[Death/Legends|late]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]—is proceeding to the hangar as well. Along the way, his liaison, [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Marsen]], informs Starkiller via [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] about the 501st's predicament. Starkiller aids the [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] by killing all of the insurgents and [[Wampa/Legends|wampas]] in the area. The [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Imperial soldiers]] then attack the remaining Rebels in the hangar while the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] confronts his former [[Sith Master/Legends|Master's]] son, a pseudo-[[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] named [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="USE" />
